title: Anduril: Access, Ownership, and the Government Gate
dek: A finite map for reporting the company without asking the reader to understand AI. It follows two separate questions: how close a record sits to a government decision gate, and how much of the technical stack Anduril owns.

history.change: Initial finite reporter briefing compiled from the receipted Anduril case.

axis_alt: Six Anduril reporting threads positioned by decision-gate proximity and stack-ownership depth. Placement is editorial orientation, not a score or finding.

axes.label: Decision-gate proximity
axes.high_label: At eligibility, acceptance, baseline, or ordering

threads.title: Army enterprise contract
threads.subtitle: Owned suite to single ordering framework

threads.title: NGC2 common-data baseline
threads.subtitle: Integration capability to government baseline

translations.question: What enters the system, what it classifies, and what the false-positive and false-negative record shows.
What action occurs without a new human command.
Which person must approve exactly what, and at which point in the mission.
Whether the government can remove Anduril and preserve the same mission without vendor-led reintegration.
Which data, interfaces, credentials, permissions, and operational state the vendor controls.
Whether the process is qualified and has demonstrated yield, accepted deliveries, and mission-capable inventory.
Which signed government decision converted a test or prototype into enduring procurement position.
